title: 48 Hours in Lisbon on a Budget
creator: Maren Abroad
description:
Two days in Lisbon for under 150 euros: Alfama at sunrise, tram 28 (and why I didn't take it), the best pastel de nata, and a sunset at Senhora do Monte.

Where I stayed: a guesthouse in Graça, about 45 euros a night
Camera: iPhone 16 Pro + DJI Osmo Mobile

Instagram: @marenabroad

sentences.t: Bom dia from Lisbon!
Part of this video is sponsored by Wanderly.
Okay, so I have exactly forty-eight hours here and a budget of a hundred and fifty euros, not counting the flight.
I'm staying in Graça, which is up on one of the hills, and the guesthouse was forty-five euros a night.
It's tiny, but look at this view from the window, you can see the whole river.
First stop, I'm walking down into Alfama, which is the oldest neighbourhood in the city.
It's seven in the morning, and it's so quiet, it's just me, a few cats, and a man hosing down the street.
The streets here are basically staircases, so wear good shoes, I'm serious.
Everyone told me to take tram 28, the famous yellow one, but I walked past the stop and the line was like an hour long.
So instead I'm just following the tram tracks on foot, which is free and honestly you see more.
Okay, breakfast, and in Lisbon that means one thing, pastel de nata.
This is a little custard tart, flaky pastry, slightly burnt on top, and they're about a euro thirty each.
I got two, because I have no self-control.
Oh my gosh, it's still warm, that's ridiculous.
A little cinnamon on top is the move, trust me.
Next, I'm heading to the riverfront, and it's about a twenty-minute walk downhill, which is great now but I'm going to regret it later.
This is Praça do Comércio, the big yellow square right on the water.
It was rebuilt after the huge earthquake in 1755, which flattened most of the city.
Lunch was a prato do dia, which is the dish of the day, at this little family place a few streets back from the square.
Grilled sardines, potatoes, salad, bread, and a glass of wine, for eleven euros.
The rule is, if the menu is handwritten and only in Portuguese, you're probably in the right place.
Afternoon, I took the train out to Belém, which was about two euros each way.
The monastery here is incredible, all this carved white stone, and the cloister is free on the first Sunday of the month, which today wasn't, so I paid.
And yes, I went to the famous pastry shop here too, the line moved surprisingly fast.
Okay, day two, and I'm doing the sunset at Senhora do Monte, which is the highest viewpoint in the city.
This climb almost killed me.
But look at that, you've got the castle, the river, the bridge, everything turning orange.
Someone is playing guitar, people are sharing wine, and it costs absolutely nothing.
This might be my favourite moment of the whole trip.
So, the budget, I spent a hundred and thirty-eight euros in total, including the guesthouse, food, trains and the monastery.
Which means I came in under, and I'm treating myself to one more pastel de nata on the way to the airport.
If you've been to Lisbon, tell me where I should eat next time, and I'll see you in the next city.
